nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock: neutral atoms trapped at a 'magic' wavelength, where the trapping light shifts both clock levels equally, so thousands of atoms can be interrogated at once without perturbing the transition. Ye and his JILA team turned this idea into the most precise clocks ever built. With ultrastable lasers, spin-resolved imaging, and control of atomic interactions in degenerate Fermi gases, they reached systematic uncertainties near 10^-18 and below. Precision improved by orders of magnitude, which created a new measurement paradigm. These clocks resolve the gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences, enable relativistic geodesy, set stringent limits on variation of fundamental constants and on dark matter, and are driving the redefinition of the SI second. This is fundamental physics through precision measurement at its finest.
